mainEntity.name: What is included in a project kickoff meeting agenda?

acceptedAnswer.text: Introductions and roles, background and goals, scope, deliverables and timeline, ways of working, risks and dependencies, open questions, and next steps with owners. Asana's version folds scope and deliverables into 1 block and runs 7, so if your project is small, merge rather than drop: the questions still need answering somewhere.

mainEntity.name: How long should a project kickoff meeting be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Asana puts most kickoffs at 30 to 90 minutes, depending on complexity. Use 60 for an internal project and 60 to 90 with a client. A half-day workshop suits very large programmes, split into sessions with breaks. Whatever the length, sharing the agenda in advance is what keeps it focused.

mainEntity.name: Who runs a project kickoff meeting?

acceptedAnswer.text: The project manager usually runs it, with the sponsor explaining the goals, and for client projects both sides' leads share it. Name a note-taker too, or record the call: 1 person cannot facilitate 8 agenda items and write down every owner and date at the same time.

mainEntity.name: What is the purpose of a kickoff meeting?

acceptedAnswer.text: To align everyone on the goal, scope, timeline, roles and ways of working before work starts, so the project avoids misunderstandings later. Skip scope or owners and it usually shows up weeks later. Scope creep. Missed dates. Arguments about what was agreed.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a kickoff meeting and a project planning meeting?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kickoff aligns the whole team on the big picture. Planning meetings go deeper into tasks, estimates and schedules, often with a smaller group. Run the kickoff first, then planning sessions with the people doing the work, so estimates come from those who will deliver them.

mainEntity.name: Should I send the kickoff agenda in advance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Send the agenda and pre-read 1 to 2 days before so attendees arrive with questions instead of reading for the first time.
